```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

```{r include=FALSE}
require(tidyverse)
require(tigerstats)
davisdata <- read.csv(file="UCDavis.csv")
data=davisdata
```
 Our Goal is to answer this question Is there a difference between the alcohol consumed between the row
you choose to sit in??

# Introduction
This is the question: is there a relationship between where you sit in class and how much you drink?
Data from UC Davis Math116 class.

$H_0$ There is no relationship between the amount a student drinks and where they sit.

$H_A$ There is a relationship between the amount a student drinks and where they sit.

#Methods

Seat is categorical, and alcohol is numerical because we are counting the amount of ounces.

#Data summaries



## Now add in boxplot

```{r}
boxplot(alcohol~Seat,data=davisdata)
```
  

The students in the back tend to drink more alcohol than the students in the front.

## Numerical Summaries

```{r}
favstats(alcohol~Seat,data=davisdata)
```

This numerical graph shows that the students in the back drink a mean of 12 ounces, almost 10 more ounces than the people in the middle and in the front.

## Inferential Tests

```{r}
model1 <- aov(alcohol~Seat,data=davisdata)
summary.aov(model1)
```
The P value 0.000116 is less than 0.05, which means the null hypothesis is failed to reject.Therefore there is a relationship between where a student sits and how much alcohol they drink.

```{r}
plot(TukeyHSD(model1))
```

The tukey graph shows that students in the front back and the middle back tend to show a difference in alcohol consumption. There isn't a difference in alcohol consumption between the front and middle rows.

## Conclusions

The question was if there is a difference between the alcohol consumption between students in the front seat vs. the back seat. The alternative hypothesis was failed to reject, there is a relationship between alcohol and seating location. The students who sit in th back consume more alcohol than the students who sit anywhere else.
